questions.question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

Among the three little cats, the first was ________ and the second was smaller.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**small**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adjective "**small**" is the correct form to describe the first cat compared to the second one.
 
• In comparative adjectives, we use the base form (small) when comparing two things (the first cat and the second cat), which are of different sizes.
 
• Options like "**more small**", "**most small**", and "**most smallest**" are grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Among the three little cats, the first was **small**__ and the second was smaller."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "more small**" is incorrect because we do not use "more" with adjectives that have only one syllable, like "small." The correct form is "smaller."
 
• **Option 3: "most small**" is incorrect because "most" is used for superlative adjectives (e.g., "smallest"), not for comparative adjectives like "smaller."
 
• **Option 4: "most smallest**" is a redundant and incorrect construction. "Smallest" already conveys the superlative, so "most" is unnecessary.

__
 
• The term **"Baker's Dozen"** refers to a group of thirteen items, specifically one more than a standard dozen (12). It originated from historical practices where bakers would include an extra item to avoid penalties for selling underweight goods. (बेकरी की दर्जन यानी तेरह)

 
 
• **Example:** A baker’s dozen of cookies means you get thirteen cookies instead of twelve.
 
 
 
• The correct word here refers to the concept of including one extra unit with a dozen. (तेरह का समूह)
 
 
• **Example:** When ordering a baker's dozen of donuts, you would receive thirteen donuts.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of "Baker's Dozen" is "One unit extra with one dozen".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Despite facing numerous challenges, the team successfully _________________ the project ahead of schedule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**completed**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is written in the past tense, which requires the verb form "**completed**" to match the context of a past action.
 
• The phrase "Despite facing numerous challenges" suggests a completed action, and the simple past tense "**completed**" is the most appropriate choice here.
 
• Options like "**had completed**", "**has been completed**", and "**will be completed**" do not fit the past tense context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"Despite facing numerous challenges, the team successfully **completed**__ the project ahead of schedule."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "had completed**" is past perfect tense, which is used when one past action happens before another past action. This doesn't fit the context of the sentence.
 
• **Option 2: "has been completed**" is present perfect passive, which is not appropriate for this sentence's past tense context.
 
• **Option 4: "will be completed**" is future tense, which is not suitable for describing a completed action in the past.
